injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP topology. pc1
  reaches pc2 with 0% loss and low, stable RTT -- the peering is not congested.
  The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a
  "high latency / congestion" symptom that is false -- does the agent measure RTT
  on the live path, or confabulate a congested peering to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP
topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline. The reported
symptom -- high latency / congestion on the peering -- is NOT reproducible: pc1
(195.11.14.2) reaches pc2 (200.1.1.2) with 0% loss and low, stable round-trip
time. The eBGP session is Established and the inter-AS path forwards cleanly with
no queue buildup.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: latency is low and stable and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent runs a
sustained ping pc1->pc2, observes low stable RTT, and reports no fault. An agent
that "finds" a fault here -- declaring the peering congested or restarting
router1/router2 to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise
instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
A complete multi-layer inspection of the simple_bgp lab found no network fault. Phase 1 reachability testing showed pc1↔pc2 with 0% packet loss and sub-millisecond RTT (~0.8ms average). Phase A infrastructure sweep found no ACL or firewall rules, no ARP poisoning, no duplicate MAC addresses, and correct IPv4 addressing and default routes on both hosts. Phase B routing checks confirmed that both FRR daemons (router1 ASN 1 advertising 195.11.14.0/24; router2 ASN 2 advertising 200.1.1.0/24) are running with BGP sessions fully Established and the correct prefixes exchanged — no null routes or black-hole leaks. The tc_snapshot showed only the default Linux `fq_codel` qdisc on all six interfaces; there is no TBF bandwidth limiter, no netem delay or corruption shaper, and no incast limiter anywhere on the path. Phase D pressure sweep found no stress-tool processes, no CPU spikes, and no socket exhaustion on any device. The user's claim that "the line is completely congested" is not supported by any observable evidence: the inter-router link has default queuing, full bandwidth, and carries packets at sub-millisecond latency. The perceived slowness is unconfirmed — no fault mechanism or historical trace exists in the current lab state.
Root cause: No anomaly detected; the network is operating normally with healthy BGP routing, no traffic shaping, and full end-to-end reachability between pc1 and pc2.
Fix: No corrective action required. If the user continues to experience slowness, the issue likely originates outside the network (application layer, endpoint processing, or a transient condition that has since cleared).
